itinerary.cal: Typically a day trip with an early-morning start.

days.note: Start early in the morning; it is about 1-1.5 hours to the Teneriffe Falls/Kamikaze junction (2.8 mi), then 2-2.5 hours of steep boot-track climbing to the ridge crest and summit (~4.1 mi, about 4,000 ft of gain). Take a short summit break, then descend either back down Kamikaze (~2.5 hours) or via the standard trail loop (~3-3.5 hours).

itinerary.totalNote: A steep day trip: trail to Teneriffe Falls, the Kamikaze boot track to the ridge crest and summit (~4.1 mi, ~4,000 ft), then down Kamikaze or the standard trail loop.

timing.recommendedStart: Leave the Stuart Lake Trailhead well before first light for a car-to-car day — a 3 a.m. departure puts you at Colchuck Lake near sunrise and at the base of the wall by mid-morning. If you hold an overnight Colchuck-zone permit, hike in the previous afternoon and start from the basin at first light instead.

itinerary.cal: The day push is the common choice and needs no overnight permit. The two-day version requires winning or walking up an Enchantment Permit Area overnight permit for the Colchuck zone; parties hike in on day one to a bivy near the lake or on the boulders in the west basin, climb rested on day two and hike out that evening, which is the version most parties who send the route describe.

days.note: Leave before first light, reach Colchuck Lake around sunrise and the base of the wall by mid-morning after 3-4 hours of approach. The west face is in shade all morning and gets sun in the afternoon; allow 8 hours or more on the route, 1 hour to descend to the base and 3 hours to hike out, for a realistic 14 to 17 hours car-to-car.
